text:
sam: Heads-up — I'm drafting the client-facing HTTP contract for failures. Need alignment on which fields are "human" vs "machine" and what headers we expose (Retry-After, X-Redwood-Error-Code, X-Redwood-Fallback). Thoughts?

alisa: +1. Keep the message short for humans and put structured stuff in headers / a stable `error_code`. Example suggestion below.

alisa: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-Redwood-Error-Code: quota_exceeded
{
  "message": "Rate limit exceeded for this route. Try again in 30s.",
  "hint": "reduce batch size or request dedicated capacity",
  "request_id": "r123"
}
```

matt: prefer the standard `Retry-After` header instead of a custom `X-` one — better for proxies and tooling. Also we should avoid leaking internal routing/model names in response bodies.

jenny: :thumbsup: Agree on short copy. For Console UX copy we should have a generic line like: "You're hitting your quota — pause requests or upgrade." Keep it non-technical.

ryan: Telemetry note: let's standardize on `error_code`, `error_hint_category` and `client_visible_error` dims. `error_hint_category` values: quota|latency|backend|validation. That makes analytics easier.

sam: Quick proposal: 1) human message <= 120 chars, 2) machine fields in JSON: `error_code`, `hint`, `hint_category`, `request_id`, 3) emit `Retry-After` header for rate limits, 4) optional `X-Redwood-Fallback` header when we route to a smaller model (but not expose internal model ids).

dev-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed /v1/error-contract at 2024-05-11T17:03Z

alisa: UX question — when we fall back to a smaller model for capacity reasons, should we return a non-2xx or return 200 with a `warning`/header? My vote: return 200 with a `warning` field and `X-Redwood-Fallback: degraded` header so clients can opt into stricter checks.

matt: 200 + warning seems reasonable. 4xx/5xx are for client/server errors, not degraded quality. But we must be explicit in docs about semantics.

jenny: For Console alerts: only show "fallback in use" if eval-based quality metrics drop below threshold. Otherwise it's noise.

ryan: On telemetry schema: I'll add `client_visible_error` (string), `error_code` (string), `hint_category` (string), and `fallback_flag` (bool) to our BigQuery table. Will include example mapping.

sam: Action items: matt to draft canonical header names + example responses, ryan to add telemetry dims + example schemas, jenny to write Console copy variations, alisa to update API docs. I'll collect and fold into the RFC.

matt: PR opened: github.com/redwood/rfcs/pull/432 — includes header set: `X-Redwood-Error-Code`, `X-Redwood-Retry-After` (backwards compat), `X-Redwood-Fallback`. Also sample bodies.

jenny: Draft Console strings attached in the PR comments: 1) "You're sending requests faster than your plan allows — try again or upgrade." 2) "Quality reduced due to fallback — see details in Activity."

sam: Great progress. Let's avoid exposing internal model ids in any public header/body. Keep machine fields stable — we'll version them in the API. Ping me when PRs are ready for review. Thanks everyone!
